paragraphs: AdaNeg addresses a mismatch in how vision-language models detect unfamiliar images. Existing approaches can use negative text labels to describe what falls outside the expected categories. However, a fixed set of labels may poorly describe the unfamiliar images in a particular dataset, weakening the guidance those labels provide.

The method builds adaptive negative proxies from images encountered during testing. A feature memory bank selectively retains discriminative image features. Task-adaptive proxies average stored features to summarize the dataset, while sample-adaptive proxies weight them according to their similarity to the current image. These two views capture both shared characteristics and details relevant to individual examples.

The final detection score combines these visual proxies with static negative text labels. This makes the guidance responsive to the observed distribution while retaining textual information. AdaNeg requires neither training nor annotations and maintains fast testing. Across the reported benchmarks it improves detection; on ImageNet, the abstract reports a 2.45% increase in AUROC and a 6.48% reduction in FPR95 relative to existing methods.
neurips-2024-adaneg-adaptive-negative-pr.tldr: AdaNeg improves unfamiliar-image detection by combining fixed negative text labels with visual proxies adapted to test images.

paragraphs: BiDM investigates how far diffusion-model compression can go when both weights and activations use only one bit. This extreme reduction promises substantial storage and computation savings, but ordinary binarization can severely damage generation quality or make generation collapse. The paper designs binarization around the particular structure of diffusion models.

Its temporal component, the Timestep-friendly Binary Structure, uses learnable activation binarizers and feature connections across timesteps. These address activation features that are strongly associated with the diffusion timestep. Its spatial component, Space Patched Distillation, uses spatial locality to make transferring knowledge into binary features easier. Together, the components address two distinct difficulties in preserving image-generation behavior.

For LDM-4 on LSUN-Bedrooms at 256 by 256 resolution, the fully binary model achieves an FID of 22.74. The abstract contrasts this with a reported 59.44 and invalid samples from general binarization methods. It also reports up to 28.0-fold storage savings and 52.7-fold operation savings. These are storage and operation reductions, rather than a stated measurement of wall-clock acceleration.
neurips-2024-bidm-pushing-the-limit-of-q.tldr: BiDM adapts binary computation to diffusion timesteps and spatial features, enabling one-bit weights and activations with substantial compression.

paragraphs: This paper proposes a mathematical model of spatial representation in hippocampal-entorhinal circuits. It starts from objectives such as representing a large range of positions and storing substantial spatial information per neuron. The aim is to explain how distributed neural representations could support useful computations within a cognitive map.

Position is encoded using a residue number system: multiple component values jointly describe a location. Each component is represented by a high-dimensional, complex-valued vector. A binding operation combines them into one position vector while preserving similarity. A modular attractor network keeps the combined position representation consistent with its components, with modules corresponding to entorhinal grid-cell modules.

The same binding mechanism can attach contextual information to spatial representations, providing a way to compose location and context. The authors analyze scaling, similarity preservation, and convergence, and demonstrate noise robustness, sub-integer positional resolution, and path integration in model experiments. These findings support the model's computational capabilities. The work also produces testable experimental predictions, connecting its mathematical construction to questions about biological spatial coding.
neurips-2024-binding-in-hippocampal-ento.tldr: A compositional vector model explains how spatial components and contexts could combine into robust cognitive maps.

paragraphs: This paper studies what happens to Sharpness Aware Minimization, or SAM, as neural networks become wider. SAM uses parameter perturbations during training, so scaling a network raises a question beyond choosing a learning rate: do those perturbations continue to meaningfully affect every layer? The authors examine this through the infinite-width limit.

Using the Tensor Programs framework, they find that standard SAM's limiting dynamics effectively apply SAM only to the final layer, even with optimal hyperparameters. They introduce Maximal Update and Perturbation Parameterization, written μP², which scales perturbations separately by layer. In this parameterization, all layers both learn features and experience effective perturbations in the limit.

Experiments with multilayer perceptrons, ResNets, and Vision Transformers demonstrate transfer across model scales of the jointly optimal learning rate and perturbation radius. This connects the theoretical scaling analysis to practical hyperparameter selection. The paper also gives a condition for deriving corresponding parameterizations for Adaptive SAM and SAM-ON, extending the idea of balanced perturbation effects beyond the standard SAM rule.
neurips-2024-boldsymbol-mu-mathbf-p-2-ef.tldr: μP² scales SAM perturbations by layer so all layers remain effectively perturbed and feature-learning at infinite width.

paragraphs: Machine unlearning seeks to remove the influence of selected training examples without rebuilding a model from scratch. The intended result is approximately what training without those examples would have produced. This paper studies projected noisy stochastic gradient descent as a way to obtain that result with a formal guarantee.

The guarantee assumes convexity. Under that assumption, the authors establish approximate unlearning and prove computational savings relative to retraining. The method supports both sequential deletion requests and batch deletion. Their analysis tracks the infinite Wasserstein distance between related learning and unlearning processes, providing the mathematical basis for these guarantees and capabilities.

Experiments compare the approach with leading gradient-based approximate unlearning methods under the same privacy constraint. The reported utility is similar while requiring only 2% of their gradient computations in the mini-batch setting and 10% in the full-batch setting. These findings indicate a substantial reduction in gradient work for the evaluated settings. The theoretical contribution is specifically an approximate unlearning guarantee under convexity, rather than an unrestricted guarantee for arbitrary training problems.
neurips-2024-certified-machine-unlearnin.tldr: Projected noisy stochastic gradient descent enables certified approximate unlearning under convexity with reduced gradient computation.

paragraphs: Visual tracking follows a target through a video after receiving its initial bounding box. Language descriptions can provide additional information about the target, but the paper identifies ambiguous manual descriptions as a major reason vision-language trackers can trail strong visual trackers. ChatTracker addresses the quality of this language guidance.

It uses a multimodal large language model to generate descriptions informed by its world knowledge. A reflection-based prompt optimization module then revises ambiguous or inaccurate descriptions using feedback from tracking. This creates an iterative connection between describing the target and observing how well the tracker follows it, allowing the language guidance to be refined.

The paper also introduces a vision-language tracking framework that uses the resulting semantic information. It can be integrated as a plug-and-play module with either visual or vision-language trackers, making the approach applicable to both types of system. The experiments report performance comparable to existing methods. The stated finding therefore supports the usefulness of generated and refined descriptions without establishing that ChatTracker universally surpasses other trackers.
neurips-2024-chattracker-enhancing-visua.tldr: ChatTracker uses tracking feedback to refine multimodal-model descriptions that guide an existing object tracker.

paragraphs: DDGS-CT generates simulated two-dimensional X-ray images from three-dimensional CT volumes. Accurate Monte Carlo simulation is computationally expensive, while faster analytical renderers can omit direction-dependent effects such as Compton scattering. The paper seeks a practical balance between representing those effects and generating images efficiently.

The method uses three-dimensional Gaussian splatting and separates the radiosity contribution into direction-independent and direction-dependent components. This lets the representation approximate complex anisotropic interactions without running complex simulations during rendering. The authors also modify initialization to reflect the properties of tomography data, improving how the representation starts from the available volume information.

The resulting renderer is differentiable as well as efficient, making it relevant to inverse problems such as estimating a pose from image evidence. The abstract reports better image accuracy and inference speed than state-of-the-art techniques. These results support its potential for intraoperative use, where computation is a bottleneck. The contribution is a physics-inspired approximation that makes realistic rendering more practical, with intraoperative application presented as a potential use.
neurips-2024-ddgs-ct-direction-disentang.tldr: DDGS-CT separates direction-dependent X-ray effects in Gaussian splatting to produce fast, differentiable simulated radiographs.

paragraphs: Diff-eRank evaluates language models through their hidden representations. The paper's motivation is that increasingly capable language and multimodal models benefit from multiple ways of measuring their behavior. Its proposed metric asks how efficiently training removes redundant information, offering a representation-based perspective alongside familiar measures of predictive performance.

The metric is based on rank and draws on information theory and geometry. Its focus is the organization of information inside the model, making it a quantitative tool for examining learned representations. The authors apply the approach both to language-only models and to models that handle multiple types of input.

For language models, the reported Diff-eRank values increase with model size and correlate well with loss and accuracy. These observations connect the proposed representation measure to conventional evaluation outcomes. For multimodal models, the authors develop an alignment evaluation based on eRank and find strong alignment under that method. Together, the results support the metric's applicability across the evaluated settings, while keeping its alignment conclusion tied to the proposed evaluation.
neurips-2024-diff-erank-a-novel-rank-bas.tldr: Diff-eRank measures information redundancy in hidden representations and relates that measure to language-model performance and multimodal alignment.

paragraphs: Federated foundation models allow clients to collaborate on fine-tuning while their datasets remain distributed. Clients can have different data and preferences, creating a need for personalization. This paper adds another concern: the inputs a client encounters at test time may differ from the distribution used to personalize its model.

The authors formulate test-time personalization as handling client-specific preferences and test-time distribution shifts together. Their Federated Dual-Personalizing Adapter, or FedDPA, combines a foundation model with a global adapter and a local adapter. These components jointly address the two demands, using adapters within the parameter-efficient approach motivated by communication and computation costs.

At inference, an instance-wise weighting mechanism dynamically combines the global and local adapters for each example. The balance can therefore vary with the test input rather than being fixed for every client interaction. Evaluations across benchmark NLP tasks support the method's effectiveness. The central contribution is this input-dependent combination of shared and personalized adaptation, designed for settings where client differences and changing test distributions must be handled simultaneously.
neurips-2024-dual-personalizing-adapter-.tldr: FedDPA dynamically combines global and local adapters to personalize federated foundation models under test-time distribution shifts.

paragraphs: EEGPT is a ten-million-parameter transformer designed to extract reusable features from EEG recordings. Such recordings are difficult to model because useful brain-activity signals can be weak relative to noise, individuals differ, and recording channels may not match. The paper addresses these obstacles through its pretraining objectives and architecture.

Its mask-based dual self-supervised method introduces alignment across spatial and temporal representations. The learning task uses representations with high signal-to-noise ratio and rich semantic information instead of relying on raw signals as its target. This is intended to reduce the poor feature quality associated with noisy recordings. A hierarchical structure separately processes spatial and temporal information, reducing computational complexity while improving flexibility.

The model is pretrained on a large mixed dataset containing multiple EEG tasks. In downstream evaluations using linear probing, the authors report state-of-the-art performance across a range of tasks. This supports the value of the learned representation for those evaluated uses. The findings connect the representation-alignment objective and separate spatial-temporal processing to more effective transferable EEG features.
neurips-2024-eegpt-pretrained-transforme.tldr: EEGPT learns transferable EEG features through masked self-supervision, representation alignment, and separate spatial-temporal processing.

paragraphs: In-context learning lets a language model use example input-label pairs to predict a new label without updating its parameters. This paper investigates an unexpected observation: pruning model weights using singular value decomposition can improve that ability. Pruning deeper layers also often produces more stable improvements than pruning shallower ones.

To explain these observations, the authors analyze in-context learning through implicit gradient-descent trajectories. They derive generalization bounds based on mutual information using the full trajectories. This provides a theoretical account connecting the internal learning process to the observed effects of pruning, including the differing behavior of deep and shallow layers.

The experimental and theoretical insights motivate a simple derivative-free algorithm that combines model compression with improved in-context inference for downstream tasks. Experiments on benchmark datasets and open-source language models demonstrate its effectiveness. The significance is that removing parts of the weight representation can sometimes improve how a model uses demonstrations, in addition to compressing it. The reported deeper-layer advantage remains an empirical tendency rather than a guarantee for every model.
neurips-2024-enhancing-in-context-learni.tldr: SVD-based weight pruning can improve in-context learning, with implicit gradient-descent analysis helping explain the observed gains.

paragraphs: FedGTST addresses how a collaboratively trained federated model transfers beyond its participating clients' local domains. The paper argues that optimizing local transferability and inspecting indirect transfer metrics can miss the broader objective: controlling loss on the target domain. It therefore makes cross-client statistics central to federated training.

The method exchanges information about clients' Jacobian norms and tunes their aggregate behavior. It promotes an increased average at the server and uses the shared information in local regularization to reduce cross-client variation. The analysis connects increasing the averaged Jacobian norm and reducing its variance to tight control of target loss, producing an upper bound involving source loss and source-target discrepancy.

Experiments include transfer from MNIST to MNIST-M and from CIFAR10 to SVHN. For the latter pair with a LeNet backbone, the abstract reports accuracy improvements of 9.8% over FedSR and 7.6% over FedIIR. These results support the proposed statistics-tuning strategy in the evaluated settings. Its broader contribution is a connection between quantities coordinated during federated training and the final transfer objective.
neurips-2024-fedgtst-boosting-global-tra.tldr: FedGTST tunes cross-client Jacobian statistics to improve federated transfer and connect training behavior to target-loss guarantees.

paragraphs: GAMap addresses navigation toward objects from categories a robot has not received task-specific training to find. Guidance based mainly on category semantics can struggle when the robot sees only part of an object. It can also lack the detailed geometric and functional information needed to interpret the surroundings.

The method constructs Geometric-part and Affordance Maps that incorporate object parts and attributes related to what objects afford. A multi-scale scoring approach captures these cues at different scales. This expands navigation guidance beyond a category-level description, using both the visible structure of objects and information about their functions to guide the search.

Experiments on HM3D and Gibson report improvements in success rate and success weighted by path length. These findings indicate benefits for both reaching the target and the path-sensitive measure of navigation success. The approach achieves the reported gains without additional task-specific training or fine-tuning on unseen-object semantics or robot locomotion. Its contribution is to make geometric and functional cues useful for navigation in that zero-shot setting.
neurips-2024-gamap-zero-shot-object-goal.tldr: GAMap uses multi-scale object-part and affordance information to improve navigation toward unseen object categories without task-specific fine-tuning.

paragraphs: The Gated Inference Network estimates changing hidden states from noisy, high-dimensional observations. It targets state-space models with nonlinear transitions and observations, where the system's dynamics must be inferred from what is visible. Its applications include estimating an object's state and filling in missing observations as a physical system evolves.

GIN separates a representation of the object from a latent state representing its dynamics. For inference, it combines a deep extended Kalman-filter approach with a compact recurrent network that computes filtering and smoothing gains. The design reduces per-step computational cost relative to the extended Kalman filter, but the compact recurrence introduces exploding-gradient problems. A specialized learning method addresses that training instability.

The complete model is trained end-to-end on videos of simulated and real physical systems. It outperforms the compared recurrent, autoregressive, and variational approaches on state estimation and missing-data imputation. These results support using the separated representations and learned inference structure together. The paper's contribution includes both the inference architecture and the training method needed to make its compact recurrence stable.
neurips-2024-gated-inference-network-inf.tldr: GIN combines separated object and dynamics representations with compact recurrent Bayesian inference for state estimation and missing-data recovery.

paragraphs: Generative Hierarchical Materials Search, or GenMS, turns natural-language requests into candidate crystal structures. The paper treats this as a multi-objective search problem: a candidate should satisfy the user's description while also having desirable predicted material properties. Producing a structure is therefore one stage in a larger process of proposing and assessing possibilities.

A language model first converts the request into intermediate textual information, such as a chemical formula. A diffusion model uses that information to generate continuous-valued crystal structures. A graph neural network predicts properties of those structures, including formation energy. During inference, a forward tree search coordinates all three components to explore possible candidates.

Experiments show better satisfaction of user requests and generation of lower-energy structures than the alternatives evaluated. The system also generates complex families, including double perovskites, layered structures, and spinels, directly from natural-language input. These findings illustrate the value of combining generation with property-guided search. The property assessment described here comes from the predictive model within the search process.
neurips-2024-generative-hierarchical-mat.tldr: GenMS combines language, diffusion, and property-prediction models in a search process that generates crystals from natural-language requests.

paragraphs: GREAT Score evaluates adversarial robustness using a generative model to approximate the data distribution. The motivation is that aggregating robustness measurements from a fixed collection of examples may poorly reflect robustness across the broader distribution. The proposed score instead represents an average certified attack-proof perturbation level over samples from the generator.

The authors derive probabilistic guarantees relating a finite-sample estimate to that generator-defined mean, including sample-complexity results. Evaluation avoids running adversarial attacks, making it efficient and scalable to large models. The distribution represented by the generator is central: it supplies the samples over which the score's global statistic is defined.

On RobustBench, the score correlates highly with attack-based model rankings while substantially reducing computation. Experiments with different GANs also find consistency between generator quality and the global robustness evaluation. Finally, evaluations of online facial-recognition services demonstrate remote auditing of privacy-sensitive black-box models. Together, these findings support an efficient distribution-oriented evaluation approach, with its interpretation anchored to the generative model used to approximate the unknown data distribution.
neurips-2024-great-score-global-robustne.tldr: GREAT Score estimates average certified robustness over a generative model's distribution without running adversarial attacks.

paragraphs: Online multi-group learning asks a prediction system to perform well simultaneously across many groups as observations arrive. Each group defines a subsequence of the prediction rounds through membership in a subset of the context space. Groups may overlap, so a single prediction can contribute to the performance requirements of several groups.

The paper measures performance through prediction regret and designs algorithms whose regret is sublinear for the groups under consideration. Sublinear growth means regret grows more slowly than the relevant sequence length, so its average contribution diminishes as that length increases. The algorithms are also oracle-efficient, pairing the regret objective with a computational formulation based on oracle access.

The guarantees cover three settings: independently and identically distributed observations, adversarial settings with smoothed context distributions, and an adversarial transductive setting. This range addresses both statistical and adversarial formulations while preserving their stated conditions. In fairness applications, the groups can represent subpopulations defined through expressive functions of demographic attributes. The contribution is simultaneous group-level prediction guarantees, including when those subpopulations overlap.
neurips-2024-group-wise-oracle-efficient.tldr: The paper provides oracle-efficient online learning algorithms with sublinear regret across possibly overlapping groups in several specified settings.

paragraphs: L-TTA adapts a trained model to a target domain using unlabeled test-time data. Many existing approaches minimize prediction entropy and require forward and backward processing across the whole model. This paper reduces the adaptation burden by concentrating updates in a remodeled stem, the model's first layer.

The stem minimizes a new criterion called uncertainty, with only minimal involvement from the backbone. It also applies a discrete wavelet transform to input features, extracting multiple frequency domains and minimizing their uncertainties individually. This gives the adaptation process several frequency-specific views of the data while keeping the trainable portion of the model small.

The method is evaluated with ResNet-26 and ResNet-50 on CIFAR-10-C, ImageNet-C, and Cityscapes-C. The authors report strong adaptation performance and the lowest memory use among the compared studies. These findings support the idea that useful test-time adjustments can be concentrated at the input-processing stage. The reported benefits combine reduced training memory, rapid adaptation, and minimal parameter updates with the proposed frequency-aware uncertainty objective.
neurips-2024-l-tta-lightweight-test-time.tldr: L-TTA adapts only a remodeled first layer, using frequency-specific uncertainty objectives to reduce test-time adaptation memory.

paragraphs: This paper uses language models to construct formal descriptions that automated planners can use. Translating a planning task into the Planning Domain Definition Language, or PDDL, can help with structured reasoning, but inaccurate translations often need human correction. The proposed approach uses feedback from the environment to automate that refinement.

The system generates multiple candidate PDDL problem descriptions and progressively revises the domain description. Interaction with the environment supplies evidence for these revisions. An Exploration Walk metric provides feedback signals that guide the language model's updates, linking the formal description to the behavior encountered during exploration.

Across ten PDDL environments, the method achieves an average task solve rate of 66%, compared with 29% for GPT-4 planning directly with chain-of-thought prompting. These results support the combination of language-based modeling, environmental feedback, and automated planning in the evaluated environments. The contribution is a translation process that requires no human intervention: environmental interaction supplies the corrective information needed to improve the PDDL representation before it is used for planning.
neurips-2024-leveraging-environment-inte.tldr: The method uses environment feedback to refine language-model-generated PDDL descriptions and improve automated planning without human correction.

paragraphs: This paper studies repeated two-player games in which one player learns from experience and the other plans around that learning behavior. The planning player, called the optimizer, knows both the learner's utility function and its learning algorithm. It can therefore consider how present choices influence the learner's later decisions.

For zero-sum games, the authors give an algorithm that exactly maximizes the optimizer's utility against Replicator Dynamics, a continuous-time counterpart of Multiplicative Weights Update. They then use that result to construct an algorithm against the discrete-time update rule. This algorithm guarantees average optimizer utility above the value of the corresponding one-shot game.

For general-sum games, they establish a computational obstacle when the learner best-responds to its history: unless P equals NP, no fully polynomial-time approximation scheme exists for the optimizer's utility maximization problem. This rules out a particular form of efficient approximation under that complexity assumption. It leaves open whether a polynomial-time algorithm can achieve an optimization error growing sublinearly with the number of rounds.
neurips-2024-maximizing-utility-in-multi.tldr: Knowing an opponent's learning rule enables utility-maximizing strategies in specified zero-sum settings, while a general-sum setting presents conditional approximation hardness.

paragraphs: This paper develops a statistical way to compare outcomes described by several variables at once. Its application to model benchmarking addresses evaluations with multiple metrics whose values may depend on one another. The objective is to make statistically supported comparisons that account for this joint structure.

The authors start from a characterization of multivariate first stochastic dominance through couplings, which relate two distributions jointly. They define a statistic for almost stochastic dominance using optimal transport with a smooth cost. An entropy-regularized version supports efficient computation through the Sinkhorn algorithm, connecting the distributional comparison to a practical numerical procedure.

For the empirical statistic, the paper establishes a central limit theorem and consistency of a bootstrap procedure. These results underpin a hypothesis-testing framework that quantifies statistical evidence for comparisons. The authors demonstrate it by benchmarking large language models on multiple metrics. The significance is that dependencies between evaluation measures enter the comparison, allowing relative model performance to be assessed through a joint statistical test rather than treating every measure as a separate outcome.
neurips-2024-multivariate-stochastic-dom.tldr: An optimal-transport test compares models across multiple dependent metrics using multivariate almost stochastic dominance.

paragraphs: This paper examines why adapting a vision-language model such as CLIP can remain difficult after prompt tuning. It distinguishes task misalignment from data misalignment. Soft prompts can mitigate the former, while the latter involves knowledge that influences predictions despite being irrelevant to the downstream task.

The authors build a structural causal model of pretraining and adaptation to analyze this interference. Because task-irrelevant knowledge is unobservable, they use front-door adjustment to motivate Causality-Guided Semantic Decoupling and Classification, or CDC. The method separates semantic information in downstream data and makes a classification based on each resulting semantic.

CDC then uses Dempster-Shafer evidence theory to assess uncertainty in the predictions produced from these different semantics. This makes uncertainty part of the treatment of potentially interfering information. Experiments across multiple settings consistently support the method's effectiveness. The contribution is a causal account of data misalignment together with an adaptation procedure designed to mitigate its effects, linking separate semantic predictions and uncertainty assessment to the downstream classification problem.
neurips-2024-rethinking-misalignment-in-.tldr: CDC uses causal reasoning, semantic separation, and uncertainty assessment to reduce task-irrelevant interference when adapting vision-language models.

paragraphs: Causal representation learning tries to recover hidden causal variables and their relationships from observed data. Existing identifiability results can describe recovery with infinitely many observations, but do not establish how finite data affect reliability. This paper provides sample-complexity guarantees connecting observation counts to recovery accuracy and probability.

The analysis considers general latent causal models with stochastic soft interventions and a linear transformation from hidden variables to observations. Recovery has specified ambiguities: the graph is recovered up to ancestors, and each latent variable can remain mixed with its parents. These define the identifiable result to which the finite-sample guarantees apply.

For graph recovery up to ancestors, O((log(1/δ))⁴) samples suffice for success probability 1 − δ. For latent-variable recovery within ε of the identifiability class, O(((1/ε) log(1/δ))⁴) samples suffice at the same probability. These are sufficient sample bounds under the stated setting. They quantify how stronger confidence and finer recovery accuracy affect the provided data requirements without claiming uniquely exact recovery of every hidden variable.
neurips-2024-sample-complexity-of-interv.tldr: The paper establishes finite-sample sufficient bounds for recovering latent causal structure and variables under soft interventions and linear observation mixing.

paragraphs: SlimSAM compresses the Segment Anything Model while using very little training data. Training a replacement network from scratch can require substantial data, while conventional pruning can harm performance. The paper addresses this trade-off by changing how pruning and knowledge transfer are coordinated throughout compression.

Its alternate slimming framework progressively prunes and distills distinct, decoupled substructures. Alternating these operations is designed to improve the compressed model's inheritance of the original model's knowledge under severe pruning and limited data. A second component, disturbed Taylor pruning, addresses a mismatch between the pruning objective and the training target to improve performance after distillation.

The reported model retains performance approaching the original SAM while reducing parameters to 1.4% of the original count, or 9.1 million, and multiply-accumulate operations to 0.8%, or 23 billion. Training uses 10,000 examples, corresponding to 0.1% of SAM's training data. The abstract also reports using over ten times less training data than other compression methods. These results show substantial compression with strong data efficiency in the evaluated setting.
neurips-2024-slimsam-0-1-data-makes-segm.tldr: SlimSAM alternates pruning and distillation to approach SAM's performance with 1.4% of its parameters and 0.1% of its training data.

paragraphs: Deep prior assembly reconstructs a scene from a single image by combining knowledge already learned by large language and vision models. The paper explores whether these pretrained priors can be assigned to reconstruction subtasks and made to work together, avoiding additional data-driven training specifically for scene reconstruction.

The framework introduces methods for handling poses, scales, and occlusion parsing. These are coordination problems: the contributions of different priors must agree about how scene elements are oriented, how large they are, and which ones obscure others. Addressing them enables the assembled priors to operate together robustly rather than leaving their individual outputs disconnected.

The approach requires no task-specific training on either two-dimensional or three-dimensional data. Evaluations across several datasets include numerical and visual comparisons, with the authors reporting superior generalization to open-world scenes relative to the compared methods. The central finding is that coordinating existing deep priors can support this challenging reconstruction task in a zero-shot setting. Its zero-shot claim concerns reconstruction-specific training, while the priors come from pretrained large models.
neurips-2024-zero-shot-scene-reconstruct.tldr: Deep prior assembly coordinates pretrained models to reconstruct scenes from single images without reconstruction-specific training.
